Terri Pickens for Idaho Governor April 23, 2026 Newsroom Update: No Spring Break from Campaigning Sunday, April 19: Over 25 people in Crouch, a Boise County town of 154 people. One-sixth of the population resisted a warm day full of flowers for a townhall meeting with Terri. Video clip of meeting available on request. Top Issues: the economy, housing costs, public land sell-offs, public education spending, and corruption among elected officials. Hot Topic: A county commissioner accused of stabbing a teen and no movement in the Sheriff’s investigation. Pickens, in her role as a trial attorney, filed a lawsuit for a family who claims they were attacked by a group that included a Boise County county commissioner, while rafting the Payette River. A teenage girl was stabbed. It happened last August, yet “unexplained delays” in the county’s investigation prompted civil action. https://www.ktvb.com/article/news/local/attorney-speaks-out-after-boise-co- commissioner-allegedly-stabs-teenage-girl/277-091c55ba-7b27-4bb4-95db- 2c381a73689e Pickens said: “It’s inexcusable for an elected official to sit idly by for eight months and have no consequences for this behavior.” Big turnout in the little town is no anomaly this election cycle. A few weeks ago, Terri greeted large crowds in northern Idaho. More than 75 attended a Shoshone County Democratic event–a larger crowd than they’ve seen in years. Next event: April 26: Idaho Young Dems virtual candidate forum–https://www.terriforidaho.com/events Contact: Dean Ferguson 208-790-4530
